title: Time, Length, Weight and Capacity
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Time, Length, Weight and Capacity. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Time intervals

Convert hours and minutes to one unit before adding or subtracting. A duration crossing midnight must include the date change. For a rate such as speed, express time in the unit required by the rate.

Measure and convert

Length, mass and capacity use scaled units. Area conversion factors are squared and volume conversion factors are cubed. Read a measuring instrument from its scale divisions, including the correct unit and sensible precision.

Accuracy and estimation

Measurements are approximate to an instrument's resolution. Do not report more precision than the data supports. Estimate first to catch impossible results, then calculate and round as directed.

Worked example: A journey takes 1 hour 45 minutes. In minutes, this is (\(60+45=105 minutes\)); at (\(60 km/h\)), that duration is (\(1.75 hours\)), so distance is (\(60 \times 1.75=105 km\)).

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Convert to a common unit before comparing or combining measurements.
  • For elapsed time, use a timeline or convert both times to minutes from midnight.
  • Label every answer with its unit.
  • Square or cube a linear conversion factor when changing area or volume.
  • Round only as instructed and retain guard digits in intermediate work.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• (\(1 h=60 \min\)), (\(1 \min=60 s\)), (\(1 kg=1000 g\)), (\(1 L=1000 mL\)).
  • (\(1 m^2=10,000 cm^2\)) and (\(1 m^3=1,000,000 cm^3\)).
  • Speed = distance/time; density = mass/volume.
  • For Celsius and Fahrenheit, (\(F=(9/5)C+32\)).

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Convert (\(2\text{ h }35\text{ \min}\)) into minutes.

    1. (\(125\text{ \min}\))
    2. (\(145\text{ \min}\))
    3. (\(155\text{ \min}\))
    4. (\(235\text{ \min}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(155\text{ \min}\))

    Two hours are 120 minutes; (\(120+35=155\)) minutes.

  2. Core:

    Convert (\(3.5\text{ L}\)) into millilitres.

    1. (\(350\text{ mL}\))
    2. (\(3,050\text{ mL}\))
    3. (\(3,500\text{ mL}\))
    4. (\(35,000\text{ mL}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(3,500\text{ mL}\))

    Since one litre is 1,000 mL, (\(3.5\cdot1,000=3,500\)) mL.

  3. Foundation:

    How many minutes are in 2 hours 35 minutes?

    1. (\(125\))
    2. (\(135\))
    3. (\(155\))
    4. (\(235\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(155\))

    (\(2 \times 60+35=155\)) minutes.

  4. Standard:

    A container holds 2.4 L. How many millilitres is this?

    1. (\(24 mL\))
    2. (\(240 mL\))
    3. (\(2400 mL\))
    4. (\(24,000 mL\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(2400 mL\))

    Multiply by 1000: (\(2.4 \times 1000=2400 mL\)).

  5. Challenge:

    A vehicle travels 150 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. Find its average speed.

    1. (\(50 km/h\))
    2. (\(55 km/h\))
    3. (\(60 km/h\))
    4. (\(75 km/h\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(60 km/h\))

    Time is (\(2.5 h\)). Average speed is (\(150/2.5=60 km/h\)).
